title: 16 · annapurna · She Who Feeds the World
lines: Shiva once stood at a kitchen door, begging for food.
He had started the famine himself. With one sentence.
He and Parvati were playing dice, and talking.
The world is an illusion, said Shiva. Even food. Nothing here is real.
"The world is an illusion," said Shiva. "Even food. Nothing here is real."
If food is nothing, then I am nothing.
The rain stopped. The fields cracked.
Every pot in the three worlds was empty.
Even on Kailash, the Ganas were starving.
Shiva watched his own children go hungry.
Then news came. In Kashi, one kitchen had opened.
A woman was feeding everyone who came.
Now I know, he said. The body is not an illusion to the one who is hungry.
"Now I know," he said. "The body is not an illusion to the one who is hungry."
Feed the body before you teach the soul. That is sadhana.
